sources: The collection identifies food, untreated water and animal contact as recognised exposure routes.
It links current annual and travel-associated surveillance resources.
The publication provides annual laboratory reports for England and earlier England-and-Wales series.
It covers regional, age, sex, seasonal and outbreak indicators.
The report uses live laboratory-reporting data and documents methodological caveats.
It includes national trends, regional rates, sequencing and foodborne-outbreak information.
The report presents travel-associated infection data by geography, age, sex and country of travel.
Its historical reporting period must be retained when interpreting results.
Food Standards Agency Campylobacter public guidance
food-safety prevention and public risk communication
The guidance explains Campylobacter food-poisoning risk and preventive food-handling actions.
It identifies groups more likely to experience severe illness.
enteric-fever diagnosis, management, surveillance and prevention
The collection describes typhoid and paratyphoid as notifiable enteric-fever diseases.
It links operational guidance, surveillance, vaccination and traveller advice.
case management, source investigation and secondary-transmission control
The guidance supports management of typhoid and paratyphoid cases.
It includes algorithms, questionnaires, clearance forms and communication materials.
The publication reports provisional case numbers for England, Wales and Northern Ireland.
Final annual reports may differ from provisional extracts.
annual and epidemiological laboratory-confirmed case reporting
The publication contains epidemiological reports for typhoid and paratyphoid.
Each report must be interpreted using its stated period and methods.
The chapter provides immunisation information for public-health professionals.
Eligibility and schedules require the current national programme version.
food, water, vaccination and symptom advice for travellers
The guidance supports travellers visiting areas where typhoid risk is higher.
Vaccination does not replace food- and water-hygiene precautions.
The guidance identifies person, animal, food, water and swimming exposures.
It links national laboratory and travel-associated data.
annual Giardia laboratory and outbreak reporting
The publication hosts national Giardia surveillance reports.
Live reporting-system totals may be revised after extraction.
historical laboratory, seasonal and outbreak surveillance
The report presents laboratory reports and outbreaks through 2017.
Diagnostic-method changes affect comparison across years.
The report presents age, sex, regional and seasonal laboratory reporting.
The historical extraction date limits current operational use.
The guidance supports public-health, environmental-health and healthcare practitioners.
It includes case-management and patient-communication resources.
cholera diagnosis, management, epidemiology, vaccination and travel advice
The guidance defines cholera using toxigenic Vibrio cholerae O1 or O139.
It distinguishes clinical management from surveillance and travel prevention.
The publication explains data-source and reporting-coverage limitations.
It links annual and interim reports for multiple imported infections.
The report covers chikungunya, cholera, dengue, rickettsial infections and Zika.
Testing, travel and reporting changes affect trend interpretation.
UKHSA travel-associated infections January to June 2025
The report provides a dated six-month surveillance extract.
Interim counts must not be treated as final annual totals.
Zika clinical, public-health, pregnancy and surveillance resources
The collection links testing, case-management, transmission and surveillance guidance.
Travel and pregnancy recommendations depend on current risk classifications.
The publication explains routes of Zika transmission and prevention.
It links the current detailed HTML guidance.
mosquito, sexual and other transmission pathways
The guidance identifies Aedes mosquitoes as the principal transmission route.
It also addresses less common routes and preventive actions.
qualitative UK population risk from chikungunya
The assessment considers global expansion and invasive-vector detections.
Its conclusions are conditional on vector establishment and changing epidemiology.
nationwide mosquito activity and invasive-species detection
The programme provides long-term surveillance across UK sites.
It informs ecology, seasonality and vector-risk assessments.
zoonotic transmission, clinical features, diagnosis and prevention
The guidance describes pathogenic Leptospira and exposure routes.
Diagnosis requires appropriate clinical and laboratory evidence.
The collection covers direct, food, water and vector-mediated zoonotic transmission.
Disease-specific management requires the linked current guidance.
diagnosis, prevention, treatment and mandatory surveillance
The collection describes healthcare-associated C. difficile infection and risk factors.
It links management guidance and mandatory surveillance outputs.
UKHSA and DHSC C. difficile control guidance
infection prevention, environmental hygiene and incident management
The interim guidance replaces outdated sections and links newer recommendations.
A further management and prevention review is in progress.
annual CDI counts and rates by organisation and location
The release contains accredited official statistics for patients aged 2 years and over.
Counts and rates must be interpreted using reporting definitions and denominators.
monthly CDI data by prior trust exposure
The release stratifies mandatory surveillance by exposure attribution.
Recent monthly data may be revised through routine quality processes.
quarterly MRSA, MSSA, Gram-negative bacteraemia and CDI surveillance
The release combines mandatory healthcare-associated infection indicators.
Organism definitions, attribution and reporting periods must be retained.
annual epidemiological commentary for bacteraemia and CDI
The report provides annual trends and organisational comparisons.
Changes in surveillance definitions and data quality affect longitudinal comparison.
30-day all-cause fatality following selected HCAI reports
The statistics concern all-cause deaths after reported infection.
They do not establish that infection caused every recorded death.
UKHSA C. difficile ribotyping network report
The report summarises isolates submitted to the national ribotyping network.
Submission patterns and laboratory coverage constrain representativeness.
current epidemiology and investigation of increasing CDI
The report analyses the increase observed after financial year 2021 to 2022.
Its findings use data available at the stated cut-off and ongoing investigations.
